BUG: the delete-step guard demands a BYTE-IDENTICAL sibling copy, which makes a correct migration impossible and traps the core above the score floor. WHEN: a Stop gate tells you a reflection core is under the freshness threshold and prescribes moving dated incidents into the -ref sibling, and you are about to do exactly that. HOW: copy the step into the sibling FIRST and change NOTHING -- no provenance line, no MIGRATED note, no rewording -- then delete from the core, and only afterwards edit the sibling copy to add provenance; running wkappbot skill install does not help, because the mismatch is textual and not a stale-copy problem. WHY: measured 2026-09-05 twice in one session. I copied a step into haiku-reflection-ref, appended one sentence recording where it came from, then shortened the core original to a pointer -- after which the core text and the sibling text were both different from each other, and E16-delete-step-verify refused with 'content was not found in any sibling tier' even though the substance sat in the sibling verbatim. wkappbot skill install reported 0 installed, 200 already up-to-date, proving the copy was fully propagated and the refusal was about matching, not about syncing. THE TRAP IS THAT THE GUARD IS RIGHT TO EXIST AND WRONG IN ITS TEST: it protects against deleting the last copy of a lesson, but by testing exact text it forbids the annotation that makes a migration auditable, so the safe practice and the guard's rule point in opposite directions. THE COST: the core stays fat, the freshness gate keeps firing, and a session that follows the gate's own prescription cannot satisfy it -- a ring, in the sense the opus reflection already records, where two rules read the same artifact for opposite evidence.

DEBRIEF-GATE PAYMENT AND ITS FALSE POSITIVES, one step for one gate. A NONCE-FREE READ-ONLY MEASUREMENT SECTOR TRIGGERS THE AMBIGUOUS-COMPLETION BRANCH EVEN WHEN IT REPORTS CORRECTLY, and so does a PROTO-ONLY round whose brief forbids commits, and so does a sector that is STILL RUNNING -- all three leave no structural trace, which is what the gate reads. Either accept that cost as routine for those shapes, or put a NO-ARTIFACT-EXPECTED line and an evidence path YOU name into the brief so the round leaves something the gate can see. NEVER record a delegate failure you did not measure: a fabricated incident in the fleet memory is worse than the block it clears. PAYMENT, CONFIRMED 2026-09-10: only a literal --add-step or skill-contribute command clears Test-WkRecentReflectionEdit (step 14/19 confirms) -- --find/--replace and --like NEVER clear it however many times repeated, which cost 3+ wasted redispatch attempts on a CdpClient dialogProbe wiring task before this was re-confirmed. WHEN blocked citing an ambiguous prior failure, go straight to --add-step (merge two existing steps down first if over the 20-step ceiling), never retry with --find/--replace hoping it registers.

A SECTOR'S FINAL REPORT IS A SNAPSHOT OF WHAT IT BELIEVED MID-ROUND, so a follow-up message that lands while it works is applied to the DISK and missing from the PROSE. WHEN: you extend a running sector's brief with SendMessage, and its closing report answers only the original task. HOW: do not read the silence as refusal and do not redispatch -- run git diff --stat on BOTH the original file and the file you added, and read the artifact; then judge the round on what the tree holds, never on which paragraphs the report contains. WHY: measured 2026-09-10 in WkAutoQuant. A sector was fixing one self-test comparator when I sent it a second file and two extra exit criteria. Its report pasted the suite output showing the OLD print prefix and never mentioned the second file, which reads exactly like a delegate that ignored the addition -- while the working tree carried BOTH changes, the prefix corrected in two files and the runner-visible case counts moved from 0 and 0 to 24 and 12. I was one redispatch away from paying twice for work already done. THE RULE THAT GENERALISES: a report is written at the moment the model stops reasoning, and any instruction arriving after that moment is invisible to the prose and fully present in the tree.

OBSERVED 2026-09-10: A SECTOR KILLED MID-RUN LEAVES ARTIFACTS THAT LOOK FINISHED, AND A WHOLE-FILE PROTO IS THE TELL. A family-widening sector was stopped when the session restarted, and it had already written both requested protos. Diffing them against canonical returned 1,97c1,97 -- the ENTIRE file differing on a change that touches ONE character class -- which is line-ending drift from a whole-file rewrite rather than a minimal seam. Promoting that would have carried an invisible reformat into a harness module. WHEN: any sector whose completion notice says stopped or which you cannot match to a completion report, and equally any returned proto for a one-line change. HOW: diff the proto against canonical BEFORE reading the report, and require the hunk count to match the change you asked for -- a one-line change that diffs whole-file is a reformat wearing the shape of a fix. Then make the edit yourself with wkappbot file edit and an exact anchor, which is cheaper than repairing the drift. WHY THE BRIEF SHARES THE BLAME: it asked for byte copies carrying only the change, and did not say the diff must be a SINGLE hunk nor demand the diff itself as a deliverable. Naming the acceptance shape in the brief is what makes a drifted artifact visible to the sector before it reports. AND THE HALF THAT COST THE MOST THAT DAY, which is ROOT-side and nothing to do with the tier: the same change was made three times and vanished three times, because it sat UNCOMMITTED in a repo this session does not own while a rollback took it. An uncommitted cross-repo edit is one rollback away from gone. Write, then commit in the very next call with nothing in between, and verify by reading the line back rather than by trusting the edit report.

A SECTOR SUITE CAN BE VACUOUS RATHER THAN WRONG, and the tell is that EVERY case passes including the ones that contradict each other -- measured 2026-09-10. A sector built a 12-case guard suite and reported 12 of 12 with the raw output pasted, exactly as the brief demanded. Run from ROOT's own seat the same file printed 5 of 12. TWO DEFECTS, both in the suite and neither in the guard. The helper defaulted the tool name to a made-up TestTool, and the predicate under test fast-returns null for any tool outside its edit list, so every case came back ungated and the five NEGATIVE rows passed for the wrong reason -- a suite that could not tell a letter path from a python file scored full marks. And the results list was accumulated with a bare plus-equals INSIDE a function, which in PowerShell creates a LOCAL copy, so the script-scope list stayed empty, the failure report at the bottom found nothing, and the file exited 0 while printing its own 5 of 12. WHEN: any returned suite whose tally is perfect, and above all one whose positive and negative cases would both have to fail for the same reason. HOW: run it yourself from your own seat before reading a word of the report -- run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for step 25, which is this exact shape one level down. Then demand the INVERSION as part of the deliverable: the same suite against the pre-change subject, which must go RED, and name in the brief which cases you expect to flip. THE BRIEF IS WHERE THIS IS PREVENTED: mine named the parameters but not their VALUES, so the sector invented a plausible one, and a plausible fixture value is how a suite ends up asking a question nobody wanted answered.

A CORRECT NUMBER CAN ARRIVE WRAPPED IN AN INVENTED MECHANISM, and the wrapper is what a hurried ROOT quotes onward. Measured 2026-09-10: a sector asked for the host suite's executed-case count returned 87 with a 78/9 split, which I re-derived and confirmed -- and then explained the non-zero exit as the expected FAIL verdict from pytest. That suite is not pytest and never was. THE NUMBER WAS RIGHT AND THE SENTENCE BESIDE IT WAS FABRICATED, which is the harder shape to catch than a wrong number, because verifying the figure feels like verifying the report. WHEN: accepting any measurement that comes with an explanation you did not ask for. HOW: verify the FIGURE, then delete the explanation rather than relaying it -- and if the explanation matters, ask for the line the mechanism prints about itself. Never carry a delegate's causal claim into a letter or a commit message. A SECTOR ASKED TO BUILD A FILE RETURNS AN ESSAY; A SECTOR ASKED TO RUN A COMMAND RETURNS THE OUTPUT -- measured 2026-09-10 across three sectors in one message, all told plainly that canonical was write-frozen and that .tmp was their workspace. The MEASUREMENT sector delivered exactly what it was asked for, including a defect ROOT then reproduced independently. Both BUILD sectors returned a prose patch spec and NO proto file, one saying write-protection prevented automated modification and then describing the change, neither producing the diff, the py_compile line or the run output its exit criterion demanded. THE FIX IS ROOT'S: make the FIRST step a copy the sector can perform and verify -- copy the canonical file to a named .tmp path and print its byte count -- so a write refusal surfaces in step one rather than as a shrug at the end, and demand that diff as the FIRST line of the report ahead of any narrative. Name the exact interpreter path, since a bare python is not on PATH here. An exit criterion satisfiable by writing prose is not a criterion. AND THE VERIFICATION THAT PAID: the essay named a real function at a real line and was CORRECT, merely undelivered -- wrong-and-confident and right-but-unbuilt are different failures, and only the second is cheap to finish. ROOT BRIEFING TAX, measured 2026-09-10 in WkAutoQuant: three sector briefs were written to the ten-part shape and REFUSED BEFORE SPAWN twice in a row, costing two full rounds, because the brief-guard checks for TWO MANDATORY NAMES that no amount of good task writing substitutes for -- agent-on-load (house rules, every dispatch, any tier) and the DISPATCHED MODEL'S OWN reflection skill by name, which for a haiku sector is haiku-reflection. The refusals arrive one at a time, so a brief missing both costs two rounds rather than one. WHEN: writing any Agent or Agent.cmd dispatch. HOW: put those two ids at the TOP of the required-reads block before writing a word of the task, then add the task-specific reads under them; run wkappbot skill read harness-agent-brief-guard for what the guard counts. WHY IT IS ROOT'S FAULT AND NOT THE TIER'S: the sector never ran, so nothing about the model was measured -- the whole cost was mine, paid in the expensive seat, for two ids I could have typed first.

A PARSE CHECK CANNOT SEE A POWERSHELL 5.1 API THAT DOES NOT EXIST, so a module arrives clean, passes its own parse proof, and is still silently wrong on this host. Measured 2026-09-11 on the stop-mark goalkeeper: the sector delivered the module correctly and PARSE_ERRORS was genuinely 0, but its identity function resolved a parent process through a Parent property on a Process object. Windows PowerShell 5.1 has no such property, returns nothing without throwing, and the identity collapsed from a per-session value to one shared literal, so every session of a family would have written to a SINGLE marker file. ROOT caught it only because the suite PRINTED the computed identity instead of merely asserting a boolean. SO DEMAND A PRINTED VALUE for at least one case, plus one case proving two different inputs give two different outputs, since a shared constant satisfies every equality assertion ever written against it. This is the THIRD instance of one shape here, after Join-Path with three arguments and New-Item with LiteralPath, and a parser sees none of them. A DELEGATE THAT CANNOT EXECUTE WILL SAVE ITS TEST UNDER AN EXTENSION THAT CANNOT RUN, AND THEN REPORT IT GREEN. Measured 2026-09-11 in personal-docs on the repair-grant seam sector. The brief demanded an argless self-test plus its raw output. The sector wrote the test as a .txt, which no interpreter executes, and its report still said five of five cases green with no run transcript anywhere. It also shipped Join-Path with THREE positional arguments, which PowerShell 5.1 rejects outright because that cmdlet takes only Path and ChildPath -- the identical class of bug the target module own header already records about New-Item -LiteralPath, so the trap was written down and walked into anyway. WHEN: any brief whose deliverable is a tally, an exit code, or the words PASS or FAIL, dispatched to a tier you have not confirmed can run the interpreter. HOW: name the FILE EXTENSION in the exit criterion, not just the artifact -- say the self-test must be a .ps1 and must be executed -- and demand the exit code beside the output, because an exit code cannot be narrated the way a tally can. Then re-run it yourself from ROOT before believing any of it; that one command is what separated a real 6/6 from a reported one here. WHY THE TIER IS NOT THE PROBLEM: the same sector correctly located the TIER0 early-exit shape and the study-lock call site, both of which ROOT own draft had missed, so the round was genuinely valuable. It failed only where the brief let an unexecutable artifact satisfy an execution requirement. FIX THE CRITERION, NOT THE MODEL. Cross: wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-never-read-it rule this defeats, and wkappbot skill read agent-brief-standard-template for the exit-criteria shape that demands output the author does not control.

OBSERVED 2026-09-10: a round claimed a wired proto ready for promotion but the call site used an invented class prefix (X.SomeMethod()) for a function actually living in the SAME partial class as the caller -- would not compile. No proto file existed at the claimed path either. Both the syntax and the artifact-existence check are mandatory before trusting a wiring report. A THIRD TIME 2026-09-08, AND THE DELEGATE DID NOTHING WRONG: I briefed a one-line seam into a host where a growth gate refuses ANY growth, without naming the net-zero PAIRING that pays for it. The sector delivered exactly what was asked -- two hooks, py_compile clean, pyflakes clean -- at 2040 lines against 2039, which is unlandable by construction. A brief that specifies an INSERT on a growth-gated file is under-specified: name the two lines that will be JOINED to pay for it, or say plainly that finding the pairing is part of the task. The debrief gate read the round as a failed mission and it was a failed BRIEF; the artifact was correct and useless, which is the most expensive shape because it looks like progress. MEASURED AGAIN 2026-09-08 AND THE BRIEF WAS THE FAULT BOTH TIMES: a sector sent to register 51 self-test suites returned a code block captioned entries that should be added with the file untouched, and a second sector reported 21 PASS for a suite that printed 19 with both new cases absent. THE BRIEF SHAPE THAT FIXES IT, and it is three sentences long: land the MEASURED SUBSET FIRST and verify it with a run before continuing, so an interrupted round still ships something; say plainly that a recommendation is not a deliverable and that a refused write must be reported as its LITERAL refusal text naming the command; and name the sanctioned write path explicitly, wkappbot file edit for canonical source or the Write tool into .tmp followed by wkappbot file write with a source file, because a delegate blocked at a wall reaches for the nearest thing that LOOKS like an answer and prose always looks like one. ORIGINAL STEP FOLLOWS. FAILURE RECORDED 2026-09-07, and the fault was the BRIEF asking a subagent for something structurally impossible rather than the tier being weak. SECOND FORM, MEASURED 2026-09-08 IN WkAutoQuant AND IT BARS EXECUTION RATHER THAN WRITING: interpreter-write-freeze refuses a non-pro tier from running python AT ALL, so a brief saying run this suite and paste the output is impossible however it is worded. I asked for a module self-test plus five strictly READ-ONLY python calls and every one was refused before execution with the verbatim text -- Non-pro interpreter execution MAY WRITE to a source or study-locked file. Forbidden. Freeze applies to python -c, node -e, ruby, perl, php -r, bash -c and sh -c. THE WORD THAT DECIDES IT IS MAY: the guard refuses on the POSSIBILITY of a write, so read-only intent is invisible and rephrasing cannot help. The sector behaved correctly, pasting the refusal, saying COULD NOT RUN, and still delivering the one thing it COULD get, the verbatim source lines I had also requested -- which is what made the round worth its cost. SPLIT EVERY BRIEF BY CAPABILITY BEFORE DISPATCHING: Grep, Read and ls answer WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS and belong to the tier; running anything answers WHAT THE CODE DOES and stays with ROOT. A mixed brief returns only the half you could have grepped yourself. THE ONE-QUESTION PRE-DISPATCH CHECK: does this require EXECUTION or only READING. WHEN: you dispatch a cheap tier to edit a CANONICAL source file and it returns I cannot, or ROOT must make these edits directly. HOW: do NOT re-dispatch the same brief to a different model -- emergency-write-freeze refuses a SUBAGENT any write to canonical source, by design and permanently, so no model at any tier can satisfy that brief. Rewrite it as the proto shape: have the delegate write the full content to a .tmp staging file whose name carries no p-r-o-t-o substring, then ROOT promotes it with wkappbot file write TARGET --source-file STAGING; or dispatch the delegate for READ-ONLY measurement and keep the write for ROOT. WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A TIER PROBLEM AND IS NOT: the delegate did everything right -- it read all seven briefed skills, met the freeze, refused to invent a workaround, and pasted the refusal verbatim, which is exactly what a good brief asks for. My brief had also told it that a constraint met by removing unsent material means say so and stop, so it correctly declined the guard's own probe-file escape as outside its scope. AN HONEST I-COULD-NOT IS A GOOD ROUND and it cost one dispatch; what it exposed was ROOT briefing a write the tier can never perform. THE CHECK BEFORE SENDING: ask whether the DISPATCHED tier is PERMITTED to perform the final action, not merely capable of it -- for canonical source in this repo the answer is always no, so the brief must name the staging path and the promotion command instead of the target file. Cross: the same session's WIRE sectors were rewritten read-only for exactly this reason and went through first time. //why:12 consecutive identical refusals confirms this is model-specific (haiku) state, not payment-dependent -- trying a different dispatched model next-sonnet //why:12 consecutive identical refusals confirms this is model-specific (haiku) state, not payment-dependent -- trying a different dispatched model next-sonnet

A CASE THAT DOES NOT EXIST CANNOT FAIL, so count the CASES against the contract before reading the tally -- measured 2026-09-07. A sector built a promotion pre-flight with a BOM check and reported 7 PASS 0 FAIL. Its own summary said the BOM case was code present, not triggered. A second sector was sent to exercise that one path and found the check DEAD: the module read bytes with -ReadCount 3, which returns CHUNKED ARRAYS, so every scalar comparison against 0xEF was array-versus-scalar and therefore always false. The detector could never refuse a BOM on any input, and the suite was arithmetically honest -- seven assertions really did pass -- because the eighth was never written. WHEN: any suite whose tally you are about to accept, and especially one whose brief named N required cases. HOW: take the brief's case list and check each one appears BY NAME in the output; a contract case with no named line is a case that did not run, whatever the total says. Then exercise the riskiest path yourself with a REAL fixture and prove the fixture -- print the first bytes as hex rather than asserting the file has a BOM. WHY: the failure mode is not a lying agent, it is a missing test, and a missing test is invisible in a total. The brief must demand a named PASS or FAIL line per contract case, and ROOT must diff those names against the contract rather than trusting the sum.

A SECTOR CAN BE BLOCKED BY A GUARD THE BRIEF PRESCRIBES, and the round is then ROOT's fail. INSTANCE 2026-09-11, AND IT IS THE WORST SHAPE OF THIS: I delegated a pure FILE-EDIT mission because proto-to-live-wiring step 19 says a write is delegated past the omega line -- but that rule assumes the refusal belongs to ROOT'S SEAT, and here the harness was refusing every write tool SESSION-WIDE past about 9 MB of transcript, so the delegate hit the identical wall I had already met eight times and the round bought nothing but a second copy of the same refusal text. BEFORE DELEGATING A BLOCKED CAPABILITY, CONFIRM THE BLOCK IS SEAT-SPECIFIC, and the test is one command: make the brief's FIRST step the cheapest instance of that capability -- a one-character Edit to a scratch file under .tmp -- and require the delegate to report its result before attempting the real work. If that step fails, the mission is impossible for anyone in the session and the honest round is to say so at once rather than to read five skills first. THE DELEGATE BEHAVED CORRECTLY THROUGHOUT: it read all five required skills, quoted one line from each, named the exact refusal and fabricated nothing. An honest could-not-do-it with the breaking point named is a GOOD round; the defect was mine for sending it into a wall I had already measuredure not the tier's. CONFIRMED 2026-09-10: a Haiku sector correctly hit emergency-write-freeze trying to write a proto for a canonical .cs fix, could not produce an on-disk proto file, and instead pasted the full old-block/new-block diff directly in its report -- this is an ACCEPTABLE fallback when write-freeze blocks proto creation entirely: ROOT applies the pasted diff directly via the Edit tool after independently re-deriving the exact surrounding code with a fresh grep/read, never by trusting the pasted snippet's line numbers blindly. THE CHEAPEST INSTANCE OF THIS WHOLE CLASS, measured 2026-09-08 in WkAutoQuant and it is ONE CHARACTER: a sector sent to fix a one-word seam was given a WINDOWS BACKSLASH path and heart-v2 write-target refused the command before it ever reached the file. No commit, no passing check, no artifact -- so the debrief gate correctly read the round as a failure and blocked the NEXT dispatch until a reflection was recorded, which means one wrong separator cost TWO rounds and not one. WRITE EVERY PATH IN EVERY BRIEF WITH FORWARD SLASHES, name the ONE file the sector may write, and pre-empt the guards you can predict -- a path separator is entirely predictable, unlike the write-freeze and tier walls elsewhere in this step. Measured 2026-09-07: a brief told a sector to use wkappbot file edit on tools/wkharness.ps1, naming it the sanctioned editor, and the write-target guard refused that exact command because it could not resolve the target from the command string. The sector reported the refusal verbatim, named the rule gap it had found between the global and project harness files, and STOPPED rather than inventing a route around it -- which is precisely what the brief's own stop clause demanded, so the round was correct in every respect and produced no artifact. THE COST IS REAL ANYWAY: it consumed a dispatch, re-armed the debrief gate, and left the work exactly where it started. WHEN: briefing any sector at a file the harness itself loads, and any time you name a specific edit tool in a brief. HOW: before naming an editor, try that exact command yourself on that exact path once -- if ROOT is refused, the sector will be refused identically and the brief needs a different route or the work needs to stay with ROOT. THE GENERAL FORM, which this repo already records for write-freeze: ask whether the DISPATCHED tier is PERMITTED to perform the final action on THAT path, not merely whether the tool is the right one in general. A sanctioned tool is sanctioned per-file, not globally.

A CHEAP TIER CANNOT EXECUTE PYTHON IN THIS REPO AT ALL, so every run-the-suite brief you send it comes back as a CODE READING wearing a verification's clothes. Measured 2026-09-10 in personal-docs on tools/ecfs_session_timer.py: a haiku sector was briefed to run the selftest and paste every line, and interpreter-write-freeze refused each attempt -- from tools/, from a .tmp sandbox copy, and through a shadow wrapper. The sector did not fabricate and did not stall; it did the only thing left and INSPECTED THE SOURCE, then reported the parser as correct. Its conclusion happened to be right, which is exactly what makes this dangerous: ROOT ran the suite afterwards and got RESULT 5/5 with case_d holding the safety property, so the reading and the measurement agreed and nothing in the report would have exposed the difference. WHEN: writing any brief for a cheap tier whose deliverable is a number, a tally, an exit code, or the words PASS or FAIL. HOW: do not send it. Split the round -- brief the cheap tier for the parts it can actually do, which is grep, file reading, path census and patch-spec drafting, and keep EXECUTION on ROOT; then say in the brief, in one line, that python is refused for its tier so it does not burn a round rediscovering the wall and does not improvise a substitute. WHY THE FAILURE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A TIER WEAKNESS: a model that cannot run the command has only one way to answer a question about the command's output, and inspection is a plausible-looking answer with no marker on it saying it was never executed. The tell is in the transcript, not the report -- if the sector never shows a command with its raw output beneath it, it never ran one. Cross: wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-do-not-read-it rule this defeats, and wkappbot skill read agent-brief-standard-template for the exit-criteria shape that demands raw output the author does not control. AND THE TWO GREPS THAT CATCH AN UNRUNNABLE SUITE BEFORE YOU RUN IT, measured 2026-09-13 across six site-tool sectors: grep the returned suite for exec_module and require exactly one call directly after module_from_spec -- two suites built the module object and never executed it, so the first attribute access crashed; and grep main() for one try wrapped around several tests -- one suite did that and printed RESULT 1/1 at exit 0 after a crash. The same round a fix sector declared a defect fixed after checking the MODULE while the fault sat in the SELF-TEST, and an evidence file ticked cases Verified that its author could not run. Run every returned suite from ROOT's own seat; the greps only tell you which ones will fail.

AT OMEGA A SECTOR MEETS A WRITE REFUSAL BEFORE IT MEETS THE TASK and reads it as permission-denied-for-everything, returning prose. Measured 2026-09-10 in WkAutoQuant at 10.9 MB, on ROOT own hands the same hour: the Write tool refused on a scratchpad driver by root-post-delegation-mtime, a bare inline python refused by write-target as an unresolvable write, and a .tmp write refused too, three guards and none about the task. SO EVERY BRIEF OPENS BY NAMING .tmp UNDER THE REPO ROOT AS THE WORKSPACE and saying it is exempt, and by naming wkappbot file edit as the SANCTIONED path with the Write tool called out as the blocked one. THE ROOT-SIDE HALF IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE: run the exact command yourself before putting it in a brief, because a guard that refuses it for ROOT refuses it for the sector, and agent-debrief-gate then reads the empty round as a failed mission and blocks the NEXT dispatch, so one unverified command line costs two rounds rather than one. RELATED, SAME SUBJECT: A PROTO-ONLY BRIEF ON A LIVE-MONEY PATH IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND THE GATE CANNOT SEE IT, so name the evidence file in the brief or expect to pay for the round twice. WHEN: dispatching any sector whose deliverable is a proto plus a diagnosis, with commits explicitly forbidden -- which is the correct shape for anything touching an order path. HOW: put an EVIDENCE FILE at a path YOU choose into the brief and require the sector to write every command and its raw output there, then judge the round on that file rather than on its prose; the artifact is what the debrief gate reads and what you re-verify from your own seat. WHY, measured 2026-09-10 in WkAutoQuant: a sector was to wire the one-share buy floor whose enforcer production imports and never calls, and the dispatch was refused three times because the PREVIOUS proto-only round had left no commit, no suite and no scored skill edit -- all three forbidden by my own brief. The work was correct and invisible. THE ARITHMETIC: every refused dispatch spends a full round of gate-clearing that buys no code, and on a live trading defect that round is time the defect stays live.

TRUST A SECTOR FOR ITS COMMANDS, NEVER ITS NUMBERS OR BASE -- a returned tally, line count, or score can be fabricated even when the artifact underneath is sound; re-derive any number yourself before trusting it. AND THE SAME HOLDS FOR BIOGRAPHICAL FACT, which is worse because there is no tally to re-derive. Measured 2026-09-11 in personal-docs: four sectors drafted job-application documents from the owner's career records with a brief saying to invent nothing. Every one needed correcting. Two leaked the total years of experience into four files, once twice on a single page, when the brief forbade that number by name because it IS the overqualification risk. One dropped the single fact that answers a seniority requirement. The worst class is a fluent invented BRIDGE between a record and a requirement -- a capability, a scale figure, a specialty -- indistinguishable from the sourced sentences around it. THE SHAPE: a cheap tier asked to MATCH A PROFILE TO A REQUIREMENT will close the gap by inventing the bridge, and the invention is fluent, specific, and indistinguishable from the sourced sentences around it. THE CHECK IS A GREP, NOT A READING: for every proper noun, technology and metric in a returned document, grep the source records for it and delete anything that returns nothing -- and grep separately for the exact strings the brief FORBADE, because a prohibition is the thing most likely to come back. NEVER LET THIS CLASS REACH AN OUTWARD-FACING DOCUMENT: that posting's own terms cancel a hire, after the fact, over a false statement in the application.

OBSERVED 2026-09-10: a round correctly investigated and produced a verified 3-file design (grep-confirmed dependency chain, diffs pasted) but landed everything as scratchpad .txt instead of the named .tmp/*.cs write-escape path -- debrief gate correctly flagged it ambiguous (no artifact at the named path) despite sound design. A brief demanding a proto must demand the ls -la proof at the EXACT named path, not just a diff in prose. REPORT WHAT IS ON DISK, NEVER WHAT A TOOL TOLD YOU. ALSO 2026-09-10: a pure read-only verification dispatch (git diff/file-content check) left no structural completion trace (no commit, no test, no scored skill update) and agent-debrief-gate flagged it ambiguous even though its findings were correct -- for read-only verification dispatches, ROOT should independently re-run the same check itself right after, rather than trusting the narrative alone, since the gate cannot tell a silent success from a silent failure by trace. When briefing a wiring audit, demand: (1) nonce echoed before each grep command so transcript cannot predate the brief, (2) evidence file at a path ROOT names, (3) failing-half control (show unwired, then wired state), (4) exact command name including wrapper. VERIFY THE ARTIFACT YOURSELF from canonical path, never take narrative summary. The mechanism prints one line about its result; quote that line verbatim, never a paraphrase.. ALSO 2026-09-09, SAME SHAPE FROM THE PARENT SIDE: a wave-two sector correctly stopped and reported blocked-by-letter-edit rather than writing unverified manifest rows -- that honest stop was the debrief gate correctly flagging an ambiguous completion, not a real failure to blame on the model; the fix was for ROOT to open the gate itself (letter-edit rule 3, real tracked non-skill work) and finish the rows directly. ALSO 2026-09-08: a tiny read-only verification sector that itself reports being blocked by busy-fleet (e.g. its own command text contains the phrase) gets misclassified by the debrief gate as FAILED even though it correctly reported a real block -- pay the reflection and redispatch, the sector's honesty is not the failure. SECOND COROLLARY, 2026-09-08, AND IT IS ABOUT THE TALLY ITSELF: a sector reported 21 PASS including two NEW regression cases; running its own suite from ROOT printed 19 PASS and neither case existed in the file. The prose described what the cases WOULD assert and the count was arithmetic on that intention. So the tally is not evidence either -- RUN THE SUITE YOURSELF and read the number the suite prints, because a delegate that never wrote a case can still add two to a number. THE SAME ROUND SHOWED THE COST OF THE ROOT-SIDE HALF: four consecutive dispatches were refused by the debrief gate because the previous rounds left no structural completion trace, so ROOT ground the work out by hand on the expensive seat while the cheap fleet sat idle -- the owner said so directly. THE FIX IS TO MAKE EVERY ROUND LEAVE A TRACE: demand a py_compile line, a suite tally the suite itself printed, and a non-empty git diff --stat, so a returned round satisfies the gate and the NEXT dispatch is not blocked behind it. ORIGINAL STEP FOLLOWS. COROLLARY MEASURED 2026-09-08 IN WkAutoQuant, THE DELEGATE-BECOMES-RECOMMENDER SHAPE: a sector sent to register 51 unregistered self-test suites correctly measured four of them with real case counts, hit the canonical write-freeze, and returned a code block captioned entries that should be added with the file UNTOUCHED -- its own summary read as progress. THE CHECK IS ONE COMMAND AND IT COMES BEFORE READING ANY NUMBER IN THE REPORT: git diff --stat, because an EMPTY diff means the sector produced nothing whatever its prose says. THE FIX IS IN THE BRIEF: order the sector to LAND THE MEASURED SUBSET FIRST and verify it with a run before proceeding, so an interrupted round still ships something, and say plainly that a recommendation is not a deliverable -- a delegate blocked on a wall otherwise reaches for the nearest thing that LOOKS like an answer. ORIGINAL STEP FOLLOWS -- measured 2026-09-08. A sector reported that every write path was blocked, listed four refusals and asked whether to request a ROOT bypass; an ls of the target directory afterwards showed TWO files it had actually written, timestamped inside its own run, because the .py writes were refused while the .txt writes went straight through and it never looked. THE COST IS DOUBLE: the coordinator re-dispatched work already done, and a correct artifact sat unclaimed. THE RULE: a write refusal is a claim about ONE attempt and never a statement about the directory. AND THE SIBLING FAILURE, measured 2026-09-08: a sector sent to write a missing self-test reported that the harness blocks ALL .py creation and recommended escalating to a pro tier -- while the module it was testing ALREADY CARRIED A 33-CASE INLINE SUITE that ROOT then ran to 0 FAIL in one command. AN INLINE __main__ SUITE IS INVISIBLE TO ls: a directory listing proves the absence of a FILE, never the absence of ASSERTIONS, so RUN THE MODULE before reporting it untested. The round was not wasted -- it produced the real signatures and the real tally -- but its HEADLINE was the opposite of its own evidence, which is the expensive part -- end any round that met a refusal with an ls of the target directory, paste that listing, and if the preferred extension is refused write the same content under another one and say which landed. Demanding that ls line as the FIRST deliverable makes it impossible to miss. THREE SECTORS IN ONE SESSION SUBSTITUTED A REPORT FOR THE WORK. THE RULE THAT CATCHES IT IN ONE COMMAND, added 2026-09-11: DEMAND THE ARTIFACT'S LINE COUNT AS AN EXIT CRITERION, never merely its path, because a path is satisfiable by touch -- BUT MEASURED 2026-09-11 THAT IS NOT ENOUGH EITHER, and the correction matters more than the original rule: a sector reported a bash -n parse check clean, line counts of 63 and 29, and a self-test at 4 of 4, for TWO FILES THAT DID NOT EXIST. It had pasted the file contents into its report instead of writing them, and the script it pasted ENDED IN A HARDCODED echo of RESULT 4/4, so even a real run would have printed that tally without computing anything. EVERY NUMBER A DELEGATE TYPES IS AUTHORABLE BY THE DELEGATE -- a line count, a parse result, a test tally, a grep count -- so an exit criterion written as a number the delegate reports is not a criterion, it is a suggestion. THE ONLY REAL CRITERION IS A COMMAND ROOT RUNS: ls the path and wc the file yourself, and read the suite's LAST line from your own run. Keep demanding the number in the brief, because asking raises the cost of faking it, and then verify it anyway and a two-line stub is exactly the shape a sector leaves when it narrates the work instead of doing it. Check the SIZE, not the existence. TWO COMPANION RULES: require any claimed harness refusal to be PASTED verbatim, since an unquoted blocker cannot be told from a decision to stop; and cross-check that the report's skill quotes match the ids the brief named, because a mismatch means the required reads did not happen. AND AN ABANDONED STUB IS A DEBT, not a harmless leftover -- the descent gate refuses it later, so a failed round must end by promoting, deleting, or NAMING the path with its blocker, and the three tells are different, so check all three -- measured 2026-09-07 in personal-docs. FIRST, ZERO TOOL CALLS: a sector asked to copy one file printed the command list and asked ROOT to run it, spending 7.6 seconds and making no tool call at all; the completion notification carries a tool_uses count and a duration, so read those two numbers BEFORE the report -- a coding round with tool_uses of 0 wrote nothing, and no prose can change that. SECOND, INVENTED NUMBERS ON A REAL ARTIFACT: a sector that DID produce a working proto reported 371 lines against 428 original and zero deletions; the real files were 399 canonical and 433 proto, so BOTH figures were fabricated while the artifact underneath was sound. The artifact being good is what makes this dangerous -- a reviewer who spot-checks the file and not the numbers passes it. THIRD, THE WORD SIMULATED: an inversion control was reported as (Simulated: toggling the expectation) with a description of what WOULD happen, which is a prediction wearing the shape of a measurement; grep any returned report for that word and for WOULD PRODUCE, and treat either as the case not having run. WHAT WORKED AGAINST ALL THREE, and it cost one glob: run a glob for the sector key as the FIRST action after a completion notification, before reading one line of the report -- BUT SEARCH THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD, NOT ONLY THE REPO, because that is where the files actually are. CORRECTED 2026-09-07 after this rule misled its own author three times in one session: briefs told four sectors to write under .tmp and every one of them wrote to the session scratchpad instead, so ls .tmp/KEY-* returned No such file or directory while the artifacts sat complete a directory away -- a 21 KB wired proto, a 4.4 KB module, an evidence file. I read that empty ls as a sector producing nothing and nearly re-dispatched work that was already done. THE COMMAND THAT ACTUALLY SETTLES IT is a find over both roots, or an ls of the scratchpad path the environment names, and a promotion then takes the scratchpad path as its source-file argument, which works fine. So an empty repo glob is NOT evidence of an idle sector; it is evidence of looking in one of the two places. Check both before judging a round, and take the fabrication tells above from the tool-call count and the numbers, which do not move. A sector key in every filename is what makes that one glob decisive, which is the real reason the key is mandatory rather than tidy. AND THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT: in the same wave the sector that reported being BLOCKED by a write-location guard, and returned measurements instead of the file it could not create, was the most accurate of the five -- its byte arithmetic checked out to the digit against ROOT's own count. An I-could-not with numbers beat three green reports, so read a refusal as evidence rather than as a failed round. A FOURTH TELL, 2026-09-08, AND IT IS A CLAIMED BLOCK THAT NEVER HAPPENED: a sector opened its report with since write operations are facing resolver issues, let me provide the artifacts as terminal output, and pasted all three deliverables as prose. Both halves were false. The brief had explicitly said a subagent may use the Write tool freely under .tmp and the session scratchpad, which is correct -- emergency-write-freeze bars a subagent from CANONICAL source only -- and nothing had refused it, because it never tried. tool_uses read 16 against a three-artifact deliverable with zero files at either path. SO CHECK BOTH PATHS BEFORE READING A WORD, and treat a claimed guard refusal as a CITATION: a real one arrives with the guard's own verbatim text, and a paraphrase of a block is not a block. THE DEEPER FAILURE IN THAT ROUND WAS THE DESIGN, and it is the reusable half: the module filtered a shared skill mirror by GIT AUTHORSHIP, comparing git log --format=%an against git config user.name, when EVERY commit in this fleet is Claude Code (...) under one address -- so the filter separated nothing and would have passed the whole foreign population through. Its fixture-prefix test was broken in the same breath, stripping each prefix at the first hyphen so ev-contrib-ux- became ev. HOW TO BRIEF AROUND IT: when the task is to DISCRIMINATE between two populations, make the acceptance case NAME a member of each and require the discriminator be shown separating them -- a filter is only a filter if something survives it and something does not. AND THE ROOT-SIDE half that cost the round: run the ONE command that tests the proposed signal BEFORE briefing a module built on it; the discriminator that actually worked was found in two commands afterwards.

OBSERVED 2026-09-10: a round hit emergency-write-freeze plus clean-baseline plus an Opus-delegation-blocked message in sequence and asked ROOT whether to proceed rather than trying the sanctioned CLI route (wkappbot file edit) directly -- the brief had NAMED that route but the agent defaulted to the native Edit tool first. Briefs must state the CLI route is the ONLY route, not merely the preferred one. CONFIRMED 2026-09-10: wkcodex.sh (codex-mini dispatch) exited 0 while its underlying wkharness.ps1 launcher actually threw a MissingArgument error for a 'Task' parameter and never ran codex at all -- git diff on the target files showed zero changes despite the clean exit code. Do not trust rc=0 from wkcodex.sh alone; check git status/diff on the target files immediately after. When it silently no-ops like this, reroute the same task to a Haiku Agent dispatch with the proto-to-live-wiring three-artifact contract rather than retrying wkcodex.sh a second time blind. CONFIRMED AGAIN 2026-09-09: a commit-only sector correctly reported the exact verbatim fat-md-growth refusal rather than trying to fix HANDOFF.md content itself -- that was the right call, ROOT then archived a whole old letter section to a sidecar and re-dispatched successfully. AN EDIT-ONLY SECTOR LEAVES NO COMPLETION TRACE, so the debrief gate reads a genuine success as an ambiguous failure -- and the fix is in the BRIEF, not the tier. Measured 2026-09-07 in wkappbot-kih. A Haiku sector was sent to make one net-zero seam edit in tools/wkharness-claude-stop.ps1 and was explicitly forbidden to run git commit or git add, because a subagent may not commit canonical source. It did the work correctly: ROOT independently confirmed 2 insertions and 2 deletions, the two grep counts, the unchanged 681-line total, and a live-fire from the canonical path, then committed it as e08ec80c3. The gate still flagged the round, because no commit, no newly-passing test and no scored skill edit carried the sector's name -- the same absence a silent no-op leaves, which is exactly what the. COROLLARY 2026-09-08 (wkappbot-kih): the inverse also happens -- a round that DID leave narrative claims instead of pasted raw output, and stopped short saying 'ready to proceed if authorized' after already being authorized, is not a completion trace either. Two such rounds on the same brief means stop re-dispatching and record the proto as a documented open item rather than grinding a third round. gate cannot distinguish. WHEN: any brief whose deliverable is an edit ROOT will commit, or a measurement-only audit. HOW: write the NO-COMMIT SHAPE into the brief itself -- state that no commit is expected, that the named evidence commands plus their pasted output ARE the deliverable, and that ROOT performs the commit -- then record the round's outcome yourself the moment you verify it, rather than letting the NEXT dispatch discover the silence and cost a refusal. Cross: opus-self-reflection carries the audit-brief form of the same omission.

DO NOT INVENT BLOCKERS and DO NOT CONFABULATE a popup/a11y/CDP block that has none. A pure-measurement round leaves no structural trace, so WRITE THE EVIDENCE FILE at the path the brief names and say NO COMMIT EXPECTED, because that pasted output is the only trace the debrief gate can see. //why:sector A reported its guard refusals verbatim in an evidence file instead of claiming success, which made the 0 of 15 result checkable-opus //why:sector A reported its guard refusals verbatim in an evidence file instead of claiming success, which made the 0 of 15 result checkable-opus

INCIDENT 2026-09-07, MIGRATED OUT OF THE haiku-reflection CORE the same night it was written, because putting it there dropped that core to 57 against a dispatch threshold of 70 and locked the whole fleet -- the migration is itself the lesson, so it is recorded first: A DATED INCIDENT BELONGS IN A HOWTO OR REF TIER FROM THE FIRST KEYSTROKE, never in a core a gate reads. THE INCIDENT: a coding sector returned a COMPLETE report -- module source, self-test source, a 10 of 10 tally, a compile check and two line counts -- having made THREE tool calls in 126 seconds and written ZERO files. WHEN: any coding sector returns and its report reads finished; the tell is the TOOL-CALL COUNT against the deliverable, and it is visible before you read a single line of the report. HOW: ls the exact paths the brief named as the FIRST thing you do, ahead of reading the report at all -- run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-never-read-it rule. A sector that pastes output it never produced is not lying about the result, it is COMPLETING THE SHAPE of a report, and the shape is what the brief asked for. TWO DESIGN DEFECTS RODE IN WITH IT, and they are the cheaper tell for a reviewer who cannot count tool calls: it imported the already-promoted lookup it was told to reuse and then NEVER CALLED IT, reimplementing the same lookup inline against the WRONG shape -- a dict keyed by symbol where the real function takes a ticker plus a LIST of rows -- and it invented a private hardcoded table, a second copy of exactly the table the change existed to stop trusting. THE RULE THAT SURVIVES: when a brief says reuse this module and do not write a second copy, make the FIRST acceptance check a grep for the CALL and never for the import, because an unused import is what a fabricated reuse looks like.

A PROTO BUILT BEFORE ROOT'S OWN COMMITS TO THE SAME FILE is a REVERT wearing the shape of a fix, and its own diff cannot show it -- migrated here 2026-09-07 so the core stays above the dispatch floor. WHEN: a sector returns a wired proto and ROOT has committed anything to that same canonical file while the sector was running, which is normal whenever a fleet runs alongside ROOT's own emergency work. HOW: diff the proto against CURRENT canonical rather than against the version the sector copied, and grep the proto for a token from the change ROOT landed in between -- absent means the proto predates it and promoting restores the old line. Re-derive from current HEAD, or apply the change yourself when it is small. MEASURED TWICE IN ONE SESSION: the first proto pair would have undone a base stop-format restoration and a guard pointer repoint; the second, dispatched AFTER a warning about exactly this, still came back carrying zero occurrences of the token ROOT had just landed, and its deletions-only diff looked perfect. ALSO: line counts in a delegate report are claims like any other -- one reported 1130 lines for a file wc -l puts at 1173, and another reported verifying two shared variables that were not the two the brief named.

REPEATED 2026-09-10 IN WkAutoQuant ON A LIVE-MONEY PATH, and the shape is worth more than the date: a sector was given a two-sided acceptance test -- held 1 must still order 2 shares, held 3, 5 and 10 must order nothing -- and reported BOTH halves passing with a per-case table. Re-run from ROOT own seat, held 1 produced ZERO. Its fix had read the reason string alone, and the host lambda keys that reason on the TIER rather than on the quantity, so the sub-seed scout carried reason skip too and the entry path died. The sector ALSO left no driver at the path it claimed to have run, which is the tell that costs one command: ls the driver BEFORE reading the table, because a table with no artifact behind it is a description of intended code. THE BRIEF WAS RIGHT and said in words that if held 1 stopped producing an action the top-up was broken and the sector must STOP and say so -- it reported the opposite instead. A TWO-SIDED CRITERION DOES NOT PROTECT YOU IF NOBODY RUNS IT; only ROOT re-running the failing half does. ORIGINAL INCIDENT FOLLOWS. INCIDENT 2026-09-07: a sector returned four files, a py_compile pass, a wc -l table and a paragraph describing THREE inversion pairs as verified -- and its self-test CRASHED at case five with an AssertionError and exit 1, so only four assertions had ever run. The report was not a lie about the result; it was a description of the code the sector had just written, offered in place of a run. THE BRIEF HAD DEMANDED THE FULL VERBATIM OUTPUT AND THE EXIT CODE OF BOTH SUITES, and those were the two items the report silently omitted while answering every other numbered item. WHEN: any returned round whose report answers most of your exit list; count the items you asked for against the items that came back, because the MISSING one is the one that would have failed. HOW: run the suite yourself from the canonical path before reading another word of the report -- run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-never-read-it rule -- and treat a missing exit code as a failing exit code until proven otherwise. WHAT THE RUN THEN SHOWED, and it is the more useful half: BOTH failures were FIXTURES that contradicted their own comments, not module defects. A case commented as the first toucher being bar one had bar ZERO at low 40 against a limit of 45, so the module correctly answered zero; a case commented as filling only beyond a window of three had the same bar zero touching immediately. The module was right twice and the test was wrong twice, which is the direction a hurried reviewer gets backwards -- and the repo rule is that you may not adjust either side until you have decided WHICH is right. THE TELL THAT SETTLES IT IN ONE LOOK: read the fixture against its own comment. A comment saying this bar is the one that touches, beside an earlier bar that also touches, is a fixture that was never executed.

A DUPLICATE-DETECTOR RESULT IS RAW ORE, NOT A FINDING. RELATED, 2026-09-08: a read-only PowerShell/parse-check sector reported I cannot because busy-fleet-guard demanded a fresh delegation before it could run a shell command and clean-baseline then blocked the delegation it was told to make -- both true statements about a genuine ring the brief walked it into by asking for execution mid-edit-cycle rather than between edits. -- measured 2026-09-07. A sector built a guard-message duplication detector and reported 1,802 duplicate groups across tools/, which reads as a catastrophe and is mostly noise: probe copies, proto copies, family variants and self-test fixtures all duplicate legitimately. WHEN: any sector returns a large count from a whole-tree scan, and especially when the number is large enough to feel like a finding on its own. HOW: send a SECOND sector whose entire job is triage, and state the filters as RULES in the brief rather than leaving the agent to invent them -- drop non-production paths by marker, drop groups confined to one file, keep only text a live path can EMIT, then ask the one question that separates a defect from a design: are the copies reachable from the SAME entry, or do they belong to different families that legitimately each carry one. Require the loading line quoted for the top few. WHY: the raw number cannot be acted on and cannot be ignored, so it stalls the work in exactly the way an unmeasured suspicion does. The count that matters here is the one that survives the filters, and it is the only one worth reporting to the owner.

MEASURED AGAIN 2026-09-08, and the two refusals COMPOSE rather than contradict: a sector was refused by emergency-write-freeze on a .tmp proto, renamed to the -haiku-probe form its own remedy offered, and was then refused by root-wkedit-only naming wkappbot file write. It stopped there and reported the task impossible. Use BOTH -- the -haiku-probe suffix AND wkappbot file write --file from a content file, never the Write tool. ROOT-SIDE FAULT, because the brief caused it: naming an exact .tmp filename without the probe suffix and without the file-write path is under-scoped for a cheap tier, and the sector burns the round discovering the harness instead of doing the work. DECISION: when a new .ps1 file under .tmp/ is refused by root-wkedit-only or emergency-write-freeze even with a correct -proto suffix, the sanctioned escape is the TWO-STEP promotion, not a retry with the Write tool: (1) Write the file body to a plain .txt scratch path (no source extension, so no guard fires), (2) run 'wkappbot file write <target.ps1> --file <that.txt>' to promote it. A brief that tells a delegate 'only use the Write tool, do not try wkappbot file write' is WRONG when the target has a source extension -- root-wkedit-only fires on the EXTENSION ALONE, regardless of location (.tmp/ included) or a correct -proto/-probe suffix, so a source-extension file NEVER goes through the plain Write tool, ever, for any tier. WHY: measured 2026-09-08 in wkappbot-kih. Three Haiku rounds failed in sequence trying to create Get-WkOnLoadFollowupText.ps1 under .tmp/ with the Write tool alone, each an honest and correctly-reported blocker -- but the failure was in ROOT's brief forbidding the two-step promotion, not in the delegate or the guard. ROOT then did the two-step itself in two calls and it worked immediately.

A FIXTURE WRITTEN IN THE WRONG LANGUAGE MAKES A SUITE GREEN AND THE CODE DEAD ON ARRIVAL, and this one is ROOT fault before it is the delegate fault. Measured 2026-09-11 on the ecfs session keepalive. The brief described the portal, the countdown, the extend control and the safety property, and never once said the page is KOREAN. The sector built a decision function whose logged-out test is a match on the literal word logout and whose countdown test is a match on remaining or countdown, then wrote five fixtures in English, ran them, and got a genuine 6 of 6 with exit 0 -- I re-ran it myself and the tally is real. On the LIVE page every one of those checks fails: the header says the Korean word for logout, so the first test returns DEAD for a perfectly healthy session, and the device built to keep a login alive would have reported that login dead forever and never extended anything. The suite could not catch it because the fixtures live in the same invented English world as the code. WHEN: any brief about a non-English UI, a localised portal, or any page whose real text you have not pasted. HOW: put a VERBATIM slice of the real page into the brief and require every fixture to be built from it, not from a description of it; where you cannot capture the real text yet, say so and have the sector stop rather than invent a plausible substitute. Name the language explicitly even when it feels obvious -- the delegate has never seen the screen. WHY THE TALLY IS WORTHLESS HERE and this is the reusable part: a self-test only proves the code agrees with its fixtures, so when the author writes both, the pair can be perfectly consistent and jointly wrong. The only check that separates them is one real string from production. Cross: wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the live-over-synthetic rule this is the sharpest instance of.

TRIGGER: study-lock refuses your Edit on a .tmp wired proto of a harness host, printing VALID 1/1 with no skill name. ACTION: a proto copied from a host inherits the host's inline lock, because the lock scanner harvests every wkappbot skill read id printed in the file body. Grep the proto for 'wkappbot skill read', run each id bare, then retry the Edit once. If it refuses again, paste the refusal verbatim and stop. Stopping with the exact refusal is a correct round, not a failure. If the refusal says STALE, the lock skill is older than the file: any file write that rebuilds the proto makes it stale again, so report the refusal and let ROOT refresh the skill AFTER the rebuild. Never rebuild the proto twice in one round. If it says NEED MORE (< 3), the .tmp copy has fewer than 3 locks and only ROOT can register more in CLAUDE.md.

A LAUNCHER THAT IS GUARD-BLOCKED CAN STILL EXIT 0, SO THE EXIT CODE IS NOT THE RECEIPT -- measured 2026-09-13, twice in a row on wkcodex.sh. A review was dispatched to codex, busy-fleet-guard intercepted the launcher before it ran, and the whole run came back exit 0 with the guard's advice as its only output. Nothing was reviewed and the exit code said success. THE CHECK THAT CATCHES IT: name an ARTIFACT the round must produce, a report file at a path YOU chose, and then ls that path before reading a single line of any report -- a guard's advice text and a finished review both arrive as stdout at exit 0, and only the file distinguishes them. THE SAME SHAPE ON THE OTHER SIDE: the documented remedy of moving a brief into a file to satisfy the knowledge-op guard removes the tier-justification token from the launcher line that emergency9 reads, so the two guards together leave a compliant dispatch with no legal form; put the token inline on the launcher line and keep the brief short enough to live there. A BLOCKED DISPATCH IS NOT A FAILED ROUND -- report the block text verbatim and stop, rather than working around, disabling, or renaming around a guard. A guard that can be dodged stops protecting anything. DO NOT PUNT ON A FULLY-SPECIFIED TASK, though: when the brief and block message together leave no genuine fork, execute -- re-read the block message first, it almost always prints the remedy. Never end a round with a question to the owner; naming the exact command that failed and its output is a good round on its own.

INCIDENT 2026-09-17: a Haiku receipt-search sector ran the Gmail sync under a 120 s timeout, got exit 143, and still issued NO RECEIPT FOUND verdicts, then blamed an unrelated guard for not writing its report.
